Healthcare AI Hackathon
Join OpenAI, AWS, JPM, Troutman Pepper, Pear VC, NEA, and Cathay Innovation for a one-day healthcare AI hackathon bringing together engineers, clinicians, researchers, designers, and founders to build products that solve real problems across health.
Why Attend?
🏆 Compete for up to $5,000 in first/second/third place cash prizes, advisory meetings with leading healthcare AI operators and industry sponsors, and 1:1 pitch opportunities with PearX, NEA, and Cathay

🚀 Connect with leaders from OpenAI, AWS, Stanford Medicine, J.P. Morgan, and leading VC-backed healthcare startups

🤝 Meet investors, founders, and operators shaping the future of healthcare

🏥 Collaborate with clinicians, engineers, researchers, designers, and entrepreneurs

💡 Build something with real-world healthcare impact

🌟 Demo your project to an audience of industry leaders and innovators

Food and drinks will be available

Presented by Pear VC · NEA · Cathay Innovation
Powered by OpenAI · AWS · J.P. Morgan · Troutman Pepper
Healthcare is the largest industry in the world, yet much of its infrastructure still runs on fragmented software, manual workflows, and administrative overhead. Recent advances in foundation models and AI agents have created an opportunity to rethink how healthcare is delivered, from the clinician desktop to the insurance back office to the patient experience.
Life sciences is entering a similar inflection point, as advances in foundation models, biological data, and increasingly automated experimentation begin to reshape how we understand and engineer biology. From target discovery and molecular design to clinical development, AI is creating new ways to compress the traditional drug development cycle and build entirely new categories of therapeutics and research tools.
Throughout the day you'll work directly with venture investors, startup founders, physicians, and operators who spend every day building healthcare companies.
Teams will leave with relationships, recruiting opportunities, and potentially the foundation for their next startup.
Whether you're already building in healthcare or just discovering the space, you'll spend the day working on problems that matter.
What Should You Build?
Build something that meaningfully improves health.
We're less interested in incremental AI wrappers and more interested in products that unlock new capabilities, create new business models, or solve long-standing problems across the healthcare and life sciences ecosystem.
Some areas we're especially excited about include:
🧬 Care Delivery & Clinical Innovation
Build AI that makes care more accessible, personalized, and effective , from diagnostics and specialty care to home-based care, clinical trials, robotics, and entirely new models of care delivery.

🏥 Healthcare Infrastructure & Financing
Build AI that fixes the systems behind healthcare , improving how care is financed, administered, coordinated, and delivered across providers, payers, employers, marketplaces, and supply chains.

🔬 AI × Life Sciences
Build AI that better predicts what will actually happen in biology , using richer, multi-compartment data to model real-world outcomes such as toxicity, delivery, efficacy, and clinical trial endpoints rather than focusing only on molecular binding.

These are examples, not constraints. If you have a compelling idea that improves healthcare, feel free to build it because we want to see it!

About Event

🧠 Cognee, Strands Agent, Docker Sandbox, Bright Data
Join us for Battle of the Personal Brains , a 5 hour hands-on AI hackathon where you’ll build an intelligent personal agent powered by your own data, live information, and create an agentic workflow to take action, all under one roof at the Web Data Loft in SOMA.
Build the personal AI agent you’ve always wanted.
In today’s world, it’s possible for an AI agent to know what you know - your emails, your documents, meetings, calendar, tasks, files, and other information that’s relevant to you - and then act on it.
For this hackathon, the challenge is simple: Build a brain. Build an agent. Make it do something.
🗓️ Event Details
When: 4:00 PM – 9:00 PM, Monday September 21, 2026

Where: Web Data Loft, San Francisco, CA

🧠 First, Build your Personal Brain
Your agent is only as useful as the information it can understand. So you’ll create an AI-powered brain that can combine knowledge from multiple sources:
Your laptop and local files

Google Drive and cloud documents

Personal email and other data sources

Public information from across the web

Meeting notes, receipts, photos, schedules, and more

You'll use Cognee ’s structured AI memory to create your Personal Brain , and Bright Data to discover and retrieve public web data.
🤖 Then, Build your Agent
Once your agent can access the right knowledge, the real fun begins. Build an agent that can find information, reason across it, and take action.
Your agent could:
Manage your calendar - Find availability and schedule an appointment automatically.

Take notes and remind you later - Capture information and send a reminder exactly when you need it.

Turn meetings into action - Read meeting summaries, identify commitments and action items, and build your personal to-do schedule.

Handle your expenses - Process receipts, extract the important information, organize them, and prepare expense reports.

Organize and share your photos - Process photos, upload them to Google Photos, organize them, and share them with your WhatsApp group.

Build your own personal assistant - Create an agent that understands your information, remembers what's important, and helps you get things done.

Connect your digital life - Connect to apps and services you use every day, read through information, create notes, identify what matters, and remind you when action is required.

Or build something completely different.
Your brain. Your agent. Your idea.
🛠️ The Agentic Stack
We'll provide technologies you can combine to build your agent:
🧠 Cognee — The Brain - Create long-term AI memory and a Personal Brain that your agent can search, understand, and reason over.
🌐 Bright Data — The Web - Give your agent access to fresh public information from across the web.
📁 Your Data — The Personal Brain - Bring your own files and information from your laptop, Google Drive, and other sources.
🤖 AWS Strands Agents — The Agent Harness - Build and orchestrate the agent that reasons, uses tools, and decides what to do next.
🐳 Docker Sandboxes — The Sandbox - Give your agent a secure environment where it can run code and perform tasks.
Together, these technologies give your agent something increasingly important:
Data + Memory + Reasoning + Tools + Actions
⚔️ The Battle
This isn't just about building another chatbot. We're looking for agents that can understand information and then accomplish something useful.
At the end of the hackathon, each team will demonstrate what their agents can do. Will it remember better? Find better information? Reason across personal, company, and public data? Can it take useful actions?
But most importantly: Can your brain beat the other brains?
👩‍💻 Who Should Attend?
Developers, AI engineers, agent builders, hackers, founders, students, and anyone interested in building the next generation of personal AI agents. You don't need to arrive with a finished idea. Come with a laptop, some curiosity, and a problem you'd love an AI agent to solve. We'll help you build the rest.
👩‍💻 What to Expect?
Cloud Credits from Cognee

High-Energy Building Sessions: 6 hours to prototype cutting-edge data and agentic workflows

Data & AI Challenges: Solve real-world problems that you and others can benefit from

Expert Mentorship: On-site guidance from developer advocates from Cognee, AWS and Bright Data.

Swag, Catering & Networking: Fuel up with snacks and food while connecting with fellow builders and founders.

Prizes & Demos: Win prizes and pitch your build directly to industry leaders.

🚀 What You'll Leave With
By the end of the hackathon, you'll have gone beyond prompts and chatbots. You'll have built an agent with:
A brain that remembers.

Knowledge it can retrieve.

Tools it can use.

And the ability to take action.

Welcome to the Battle of the Personal Brains.
🧠 Build your brain. Build your agent. Enter the battle.
Event Terms & Consent
By registering, you agree to the event terms and conditions. Cognee reserves the right to refuse admission or remove attendees at its discretion to keep things safe and enjoyable for everyone.
Photography and video recording will take place throughout the evening and may be used by Cognee and Bright Data for future marketing, promotional, and community content. By registering, you also consent to receiving the Cognee newsletter and updates about future events at the email address you provide. You can unsubscribe anytime via the link in any email.
Spots are limited. Register now and build the future of Personal Brains.

From Agentic Coding to Agentic Engineering
Qoder is an AI-native development platform designed for a new generation of software development where AI moves beyond code assistance toward autonomous execution.
Instead of simply generating snippets of code, Qoder enables developers to collaborate with AI agents across the development lifecycle — understanding codebases, planning tasks, implementing features, testing solutions, and working through longer, more complex engineering workflows.

The Graph Database for Intelligent, Connected Applications
Neo4j is the world's leading graph database, purpose-built for working with highly connected data. Instead of storing information in isolated rows and tables, Neo4j models data as nodes and relationships — making it a natural fit for knowledge graphs, recommendation engines, fraud detection, and the memory and reasoning layers behind modern AI agents.
As AI agents take on more complex tasks, they need a way to store context, connect facts, and retrieve relevant knowledge. With graph-powered retrieval (GraphRAG) and native vector search, Neo4j helps builders give their agents structured, queryable memory — so they can reason over relationships, not just retrieve isolated snippets.
At this hackathon, you'll have the chance to explore how graph-native data can make your AI projects smarter, more grounded, and more connected.

Join developers, researchers, and builders for the upcoming ExecuTorch Hackathon on October 17 -18 at Founder’s Inc., officially part of Open Source AI Week 2026 .
Hosted in collaboration with Qualcomm , Meta , GitHub , the PyTorch Foundation , and Open Intelligence Foundation , this hands-on event will challenge teams to build innovative AI experiences powered by ExecuTorch —an open-source framework for deploying and running PyTorch models efficiently on edge and on-device hardware.
Participants will work in teams of 3–5 people and select one of three tracks outlined below. Each team will receive a device from their selected track to use during the event. Builders will also get access to GitHub Copilot Pro+ to support their builds.
Compute Track
Build AI applications optimized for the Copilot+ PC powered by Snapdragon® X Elite processors, exploring the potential of powerful, efficient on-device AI computing.
Mobile + XR Track
Create AI-powered experiences for the Samsung Galaxy S25 Ultra powered by Snapdragon 8 Elite and Samsung Galaxy XR powered by Snapdragon® XR2+ Gen 2 processor, with a focus on mobile intelligence, immersive interaction, and multimodal applications.
IoT Track
Develop intelligent edge and embedded applications using the Arduino ® VENTUNO™ Q boards , combining on-device AI with real-time sensing, control, and connected experiences.
To participate, interested teams must select a track, form a team of 3–5, and submit a project proposal by October 4. Selected teams will be announced by October 7.
Prizes
The top team in each track will receive a prize package for every member of the team: Meta AI glasses and an Arduino® UNO™ Q. Build a standout project, demonstrate the potential of on-device AI, and take home hardware to continue exploring the edge.

GitHub will also award a one-year subscription to Copilot Pro to the winner.
Whether you are an experienced edge AI developer or eager to explore the future of open-source, on-device intelligence, the ExecuTorch Hackathon is an opportunity to collaborate, experiment, and build with the latest hardware and software across compute, mobile, XR, and IoT.

About Event

Build open agents that work together

The Collaborative Agent Hackathon is a one-day event for building open-source, collaborative AI agents using Flower.
Agents are changing what is possible, and their greatest potential emerges when they collaborate safely in human-supervised multi-agent teams.
Participants will form teams on the day, develop a working prototype and present it at the end of the event. Each team will explore how open-source collaborative agents of varying complexity can work together safely.
You do not need an existing team or a fully developed idea. Bring your laptop, your interests and a willingness to collaborate.
The hackathon challenge
Build an open-source agent or multi-agent system using Flower in which the safe collaboration of agent teams is central to the solution.
Projects can range across the full collaborative spectrum. Multiple agents might:
Automate a task

Form self-improving loops with one another

Operate across distributed machines and datasets

Flower is built together with an open-source community spanning more than 7k users world-wide. Flower simplifies building multi-agent systems, supporting distributed coordination, collaborative learning and inference, and privacy-aware deployment.

Projects from all industries and application areas are welcome — including scientific research, healthcare, finance, education, public services, software development and entirely new forms of human-agent collaboration.
Team formation
Participants register individually.
Teams of two to four people will be formed during the morning, unless formed earlier . The organisers will help participants find teammates with complementary interests and experience.
Already know your team? Please provide your teammates’ names when registering.
Bringing an idea is optional.
Eligibility: Everyone is welcome, including builders from startups and companies, as well as students, researchers, and postdocs from all universities.
Awards
Awards will be presented at the end of the day to recognise outstanding projects and contributions.
Further details about prizes and the selection process will be shared before the event.

Build It. Test It. Prove It.
Smells like a hackathon. Runs like a pressure test, on you, not just your idea.
Proving Ground runs a three-day Sprint where judges push past the pitch. No script survives real questions about what you tried, what broke, and what you changed.
Past teams have gone on to raise from 500 Global and Blitzscaling Ventures, and been accepted into Berkeley SkyDeck and Confluent's accelerator, independently, without Proving Ground's involvement in those decisions.
What this is
A hackathon judges what you built by the end. We watch during the process and look past the end to what may come next.

The team is almost everything. How you make decisions under pressure, how you handle a setback, how you treat each other when something breaks. You'll document that as you go. What we ask you to show and how we question it are built around behavior, not performance.
How it works
Over three days, founders build under real constraint. No script, no rehearsed demo. Judges probe what you tried, what broke, and what you changed, and compare where you started to where you ended.
Two Tracks
Discovery Track. Pre-market, no active customer contact yet. For the startup curious, including enterprise folks seriously exploring a leap.
Pre-seed Track. In-market, already talking to customers. Ship something real, show what's changed, pressure-test your next move.
After the Sprint
Select teams get invited into the Street Test: 30 days back in the real world, no artificial deadline, no audience. This is where we see if momentum was real or borrowed from the room. It's the part a hackathon can't offer, because a hackathon ends when the weekend does.
